blocks.text: Practice short questions for the whole of Unit 13 (Differentiation), arranged by the unit's sections, in the style of a 2-mark Board short question. Each one is solved briefly, step by step.
13.1 Tangent to a Curve at a Point

blocks.prompt: 1 Define a secant line of a curve and write the slope of the secant through the points with x-coordinates \(x\) and \(x + \delta x\) on \(y = f(x)\).
blocks.explanation: A secant is a line that cuts a curve in two points. Through \(P(x, f(x))\) and \(Q(x + \delta x, f(x + \delta x))\): \(m_{\text{sec}} = \dfrac{f(x+\delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\).

book_ref.quote: A secant cuts a curve at two points

blocks.prompt: 2 Write the slope of the tangent to \(y = f(x)\) at \(P(x, f(x))\) as a limit, and say how it is related to the secant.
blocks.explanation: \(m_{\text{tan}} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+\delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). As \(\delta x \to 0\), \(Q\) approaches \(P\) and the secant \(PQ\) becomes the tangent \(PT\); so \(m_{\text{tan}}\) is the limit of \(m_{\text{sec}}\).

book_ref.quote: the secant line becomes the tangent line

blocks.prompt: 3 Find the slope of the secant to \(f(x) = x^{2} - 4x\) through the points where \(x = 1\) and \(x = 4\).

book_ref.quote: every derivative is a limit

blocks.prompt: 4 Using the limit for \(m_{\text{tan}}\), find the gradient of the tangent to \(f(x) = x^{2} + 4\) at the point \((2, 8)\).
blocks.explanation: Put \(x = 2\) in the limit and cancel \(\delta x\).

book_ref.quote: Working pattern: substitute, expand, cancel the common factor

blocks.prompt: 5 The tangent to \(f(x) = x^{2} + 4\) at \((2, 8)\) has slope \(4\). Find its equation.

blocks.prompt: 12 Write the notations for the derivative of \(y = f(x)\) used by Leibniz, Newton, Lagrange and Euler.
blocks.explanation: All four mean the same derivative of \(y = f(x)\).

blocks.prompt: 13 Is \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) a quotient of \(dy\) and \(dx\)? Explain.
blocks.explanation: No. \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) is one symbol for \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x}\), the derivative of \(y\) with respect to \(x\). It is also written \(y'\).

book_ref.quote: and here it is not a quotient of

blocks.text: 13.3.2 Finding f'(x) by Definition of Derivative

blocks.prompt: 16 Write the four steps for finding \(f'(x)\) by definition.
blocks.explanation: Step I: find \(f(x + \delta x)\). Step II: simplify \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\). Step III: divide by \(\delta x\) and simplify. Step IV: find \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+\delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\).

book_ref.quote: can be found by the following four steps

blocks.prompt: 17 Find by definition the derivative of \(f(x) = 4x - 7\).
blocks.explanation: \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = 4(x + \delta x) - 7 - (4x - 7) = 4\delta x\); \(\dfrac{4\delta x}{\delta x} = 4\); \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} 4 = 4\).

book_ref.quote: The method of finding derivatives by this process is called differentiation by definition

blocks.prompt: 18 Find by definition the derivative of \(f(x) = x^{2} - 5x\).
blocks.explanation: Four steps; the \(x^{2}\) and \(-5x\) terms cancel.

book_ref.quote: Expand \((x+\delta x)^{n}\), cancel, take out \(\delta x\)

blocks.prompt: 19 Find by definition the derivative of \(f(x) = \dfrac{3}{x}\), \(x \ne 0\).
blocks.explanation: Take a common denominator, then cancel \(\delta x\).

book_ref.quote: Common denominator, then factorize

steps: \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = \dfrac{3}{x + \delta x} - \dfrac{3}{x} = \dfrac{3x - 3(x + \delta x)}{x(x + \delta x)} = \dfrac{-3\delta x}{x(x + \delta x)}\)

blocks.prompt: 20 Find by definition the derivative of \(f(x) = 2\sqrt{x}\), \(x > 0\).

book_ref.quote: Whenever a square root appears in the numerator of the difference quotient, rationalize the numerator

blocks.prompt: 21 Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) at \(x = 1\) by ab-initio method if \(y = \dfrac{1}{x + 1}\).
blocks.explanation: Find \(\delta y\) with a common denominator, divide, take the limit, then put \(x = 1\).

book_ref.quote: With fractions, the key algebra move is taking a common denominator.

blocks.prompt: 22 Why must \(\delta x\) be cancelled before letting \(\delta x \to 0\) in Step III?
blocks.explanation: Putting \(\delta x = 0\) before simplifying gives \(\frac{0}{0}\), which has no value. Since \(\delta x \ne 0\) while it approaches \(0\), we may cancel it first; then the limit can be taken.

blocks.prompt: 23 State the power rule. For which values of n does the unit prove it?
blocks.explanation: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\). It is proved for \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\): positive integers (binomial theorem) and negative integers (\(n = -m\)). It also holds for rational powers; the proof for \(n \in \mathbb{Q} - \mathbb{Z}\) is left as an exercise.

blocks.prompt: 27 Using the binomial theorem, find \(\delta y\) for \(y = x^{4}\) and hence \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).
blocks.explanation: \(\delta y = (x + \delta x)^{4} - x^{4} = 4x^{3}\delta x + 6x^{2}(\delta x)^{2} + 4x(\delta x)^{3} + (\delta x)^{4}\); \(\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x} = 4x^{3} + 6x^{2}\delta x + 4x(\delta x)^{2} + (\delta x)^{3} \to 4x^{3}\).

blocks.prompt: 28 Can the power rule be used to differentiate \(2^{x}\)? Give a reason.
blocks.explanation: No. The power rule \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\) works only for \(x^{n}\) with a constant power \(n\). In \(2^{x}\) the variable is in the power.

book_ref.quote: Using the power rule for \(a^{x}\) (variable in the power)

blocks.prompt: 29 State the relation between continuity and differentiability of a function at a point.
blocks.explanation: If a function is differentiable at a point, it must also be continuous there. The reverse is not necessarily true: \(f(x) = |x|\) is continuous at \(x = 0\) but not differentiable there.

book_ref.quote: differentiability implies continuity, but the reverse is not necessarily true

blocks.prompt: 31 Is \(f(x) = |x + 3|\) differentiable at \(x = -3\)? Give a reason.
blocks.explanation: \(\dfrac{f(-3 + \delta x) - f(-3)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{|\delta x|}{\delta x}\): right-hand limit \(1\), left-hand limit \(-1\). They differ, so \(f'(-3)\) does not exist: not differentiable at \(x = -3\).

book_ref.quote: The right hand and left hand limits are not equal

blocks.prompt: 32 Why is there no tangent line to the graph of \(f(x) = |x|\) at the origin?
blocks.explanation: At \(O\) the graph has a sharp corner: slope \(-1\) on the left (\(y = -x\)) and \(1\) on the right (\(y = x\)). A tangent needs one definite slope, but \(f'(0)\) does not exist.

blocks.prompt: 40 State the product rule and the quotient rule of differentiation.
blocks.explanation: Product rule: \([f(x)g(x)]' = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x)\). Quotient rule (\(g(x) \ne 0\)): \(\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)' = \dfrac{f'(x)g(x) - f(x)g'(x)}{[g(x)]^{2}}\).

book_ref.quote: Now we will prove other important formulas (or rules)

blocks.prompt: 41 Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) if \(y = \dfrac{x^{3} - 1}{x - 1}\), \(x \ne 1\).
blocks.explanation: Simplify first: \(y = \dfrac{(x - 1)(x^{2} + x + 1)}{x - 1} = x^{2} + x + 1\). So \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x + 1\).

book_ref.quote: Simplifying first (Examples 8, 9) or using the product rule (Example 10) gives the same answer
